Role (one line): Material 3 Expressive split button (two segments: leading action + trailing menu trigger) — forked so the dropdown is positioned edge-aware from the trailing segment's real rect instead of snapping to the screen's left edge.

Vendored fork of upstream split_button_m3e 0.2.1. The patched source lives in this repo at packages/split_button_m3e/lib/src/split_button.dart. The patch is activated by the root pubspec.yaml dependency_overrides path: entry — remove that entry and flutter pub get silently reverts to upstream.

Overview & role

split_button_m3e is a leaf Material 3 Expressive UI widget package. Hexagonal / domain-layer concerns are N/A — it has no data, service, or routing surface. It renders a two-segment button and consumes m3e_design tokens.

This package is one of four vendored forks of EmilyMoonstone/material_3_expressive pinned in this repo (alongside fab_m3e, navigation_rail_m3e, toolbar_m3e). It is the only one of the four that ships both a test/ and an example/ directory.

What this is

A vendored fork of upstream split_button_m3e 0.2.1. The fork is pulled in transitively via the m3e_collection umbrella package, and activated by a path: dependency_overrides entry in the root pubspec.yaml. The patched file is packages/split_button_m3e/lib/src/split_button.dart (the _menuPosition() method). The patch marker in source is // Patched (vendored fork).

Glossary

  • Fork — a vendored copy of an upstream package, edited in-tree, pinned by a path: override.
  • Override — the dependency_overrides: block in the root pubspec.yaml that forces pub to resolve this package from a local folder instead of pub.dev.
  • Patch marker — an inline comment tag (// Patched (vendored fork), // Fork patch:, or // PATCH) that flags every block of code changed from upstream. Audit with grep -rEn 'FORK|fork patch|PATCH|vendored' packages/split_button_m3e/lib.
  • Re-sync — the procedure for re-applying this fork's patches onto a newer upstream version (see §9).
  • M3E — Material 3 Expressive, the motion/shape system this widget implements.
  • Trailing segment — the chevron half of the split button; the menu trigger. Has its own GlobalKey (_trailingKey) so the fork can read its real RenderBox rect.

The fork contract (shared)

Every vendored fork in this repo carries the same contract:

  • The WHY is documented in the root pubspec.yaml dependency_overrides comment block above each path: entry. Read it before editing.
  • The HOW is flagged in source with // Patched (vendored fork), // Fork patch:, or // PATCH. Every changed block has a marker.
  • The audit command is grep -rEn 'FORK|fork patch|PATCH|vendored' packages/<name>/lib — re-run after every edit and before every re-sync.
  • The doc-gap checklist (every fork carries this debt): add a > Vendored fork of upstream <name> <version> banner to the README; backfill the CHANGELOG; fix the EmilyMonestone → EmilyMoonstone typo in issue_tracker (present in every fork's pubspec.yaml).
  • The test contract: every fork SHOULD ship a test/. navigation_rail_m3e currently has NONE (highest debt); the other three forks do ship one.

Public API reference

The barrel lib/split_button_m3e.dart exports three files. SplitButtonM3E is generic on the menu value type <T>. The fork only changes the _menuPosition() private method; the public signatures are unchanged from upstream.

SplitButtonM3E

packages/split_button_m3e/lib/src/split_button.dart

class SplitButtonM3E<T> extends StatefulWidget {
  const SplitButtonM3E({
    super.key,
    this.shape = SplitButtonM3EShape.round,
    this.size = SplitButtonM3ESize.sm,
    this.emphasis = SplitButtonM3EEmphasis.filled,
    this.label,
    this.leadingIcon,
    this.onPressed,
    required this.items,
    this.onSelected,
    this.trailingAlignment = SplitButtonM3ETrailingAlignment.opticalCenter,
    this.leadingTooltip,
    this.trailingTooltip,
    this.enabled = true,
    this.menuBuilder,
  });

  final SplitButtonM3EShape shape;
  final SplitButtonM3ESize size;
  final SplitButtonM3EEmphasis emphasis;
  final String? label;
  final IconData? leadingIcon;
  final VoidCallback? onPressed;
  final List<SplitButtonM3EItem<T>>? items;
  final List<PopupMenuEntry<T>> Function(BuildContext)? menuBuilder;
  final ValueChanged<T>? onSelected;
  final SplitButtonM3ETrailingAlignment trailingAlignment;
  final bool enabled;
}
  • Generic L1: SplitButtonM3E — T is the menu value type. Items are SplitButtonM3EItem.
  • shape / size / emphasis L3-5: Tokens-driven; pressed morph uses tokens. Unchanged from upstream.
  • items xor menuBuilder L11: Provide a static list (items) OR a builder that returns PopupMenuEntry. Asserted at construction.
  • trailingAlignment L16: Chevron alignment strategy (e.g. opticalCenter). Unchanged from upstream.

SplitButtonM3EItem

packages/split_button_m3e/lib/src/menu_items.dart

class SplitButtonM3EItem<T> {
  const SplitButtonM3EItem({
    required this.value,
    required this.child,
    this.enabled = true,
  });

  final T value;
  final Object child; // Widget or plain string; the caller builds PopupMenuItem
  final bool enabled;
}
  • child L7: Object — Widget or plain string. The fork's _openMenu builds the PopupMenuItem and styles disabled children at 0.38 alpha.

Enums

SplitButtonM3EShape — round / square (resting outer shape; pressed morph uses tokens). SplitButtonM3ESize — XS / S / SM / M / L / XL. SplitButtonM3EEmphasis — filled / tonal / outlined / elevated. SplitButtonM3ETrailingAlignment — chevron alignment (e.g. opticalCenter).

All unchanged from upstream.

_menuPosition (the patch)

packages/split_button_m3e/lib/src/split_button.dart

RelativeRect _menuPosition(BuildContext context) {
  final RenderBox overlay =
      Overlay.of(context).context.findRenderObject() as RenderBox;
  final BuildContext? tCtx = _trailingKey.currentContext;
  RenderBox? targetBox = tCtx?.findRenderObject() as RenderBox?;
  targetBox ??= context.findRenderObject() as RenderBox?;
  // ... targetRect from targetBox.localToGlobal + size

  const double _kMenuVerticalOffset = 8.0;
  const double _kMenuScreenPadding = 8.0;
  final EdgeInsets safe = MediaQuery.paddingOf(Overlay.of(context).context);
  final double estHeight =
      (widget.items?.length ?? 0) * kMinInteractiveDimension + 16.0;
  final double fitBottom = overlay.size.height - _kMenuScreenPadding - safe.bottom;
  final bool below =
      targetRect.bottom + _kMenuVerticalOffset + estHeight <= fitBottom;
  final double top = below
      ? targetRect.bottom + _kMenuVerticalOffset
      : (targetRect.top - estHeight - _kMenuVerticalOffset);
  // ... _menuMaxHeight side-effect

  // Patched (vendored fork): pass the true trailing rect so showMenu is edge-aware.
  final double left = targetRect.left;
  final double right = overlay.size.width - targetRect.right;
  return RelativeRect.fromLTRB(left, top, right, overlay.size.height);
}
  • overlay context L2-3: Read MediaQuery.paddingOf from Overlay.of(context).context — that's where showMenu reads it. A Scaffold body can consume padding; reading from the button's context would under-count the bottom nav/safe-area.
  • trailing rect L4-6: Prefer the trailing segment's RenderBox (_trailingKey); fall back to the whole control. This is the rect that anchors the menu.
  • 8px gap L9: Was 4 upstream. 8 matches KitNativePopupMenu so both dropdowns sit the same distance below their trigger.
  • flip above L13-15: If the menu does not fit below (using the same screen-fit bound showMenu uses), flip it above the trigger.
  • edge-aware left/right L22-24: THE PATCH. Upstream pinned left=0.0 in LTR so _PopupMenuRouteLayout always picked the left side. Passing the real rect lets showMenu right-align for right-of-centre triggers and left-align for left-of-centre.

Usage playbook

example/split_usage.dart

import 'package:m3e_collection/m3e_collection.dart';

SplitButtonM3E<String>(
  label: 'Send',
  leadingIcon: Icons.send,
  onPressed: () => _send(),
  onSelected: (v) => _sendAs(v),
  items: [
    SplitButtonM3EItem(value: 'plain', child: 'Plain'),
    SplitButtonM3EItem(value: 'encrypted', child: 'Encrypted'),
  ],
)
  • generic L2: SplitButtonM3E — T flows through items, onSelected, and the PopupMenuEntry list.
  • items L7-10: SplitButtonM3EItem.child accepts a Widget or a plain string; the fork's _openMenu builds the PopupMenuItem and applies disabled-alpha styling.

5b. Wiring — how a host actually gets this fork

pubspec.yaml (root)

# Vendored fork of split_button_m3e 0.2.1 (pulled in via m3e_collection).
# Patched so the dropdown is positioned edge-aware from the trigger's real rect
# (right-aligned for a right-side trigger, left for a left one) instead of
# snapping to the screen's left edge. Patch: packages/split_button_m3e/lib/src/
# split_button.dart _menuPosition.
dependency_overrides:
  split_button_m3e:
    path: packages/split_button_m3e
  • WHY L1-4: Root pubspec.yaml override comment. This is the auditable reason for the fork; edit it whenever the patch changes.
  • HOW L5-7: path: override activates the fork. m3e_collection still re-exports split_button_m3e by name; the override redirects that name to the local folder.

Hosts almost never import package:split_button_m3e/... directly. The fork is pulled in transitively via m3e_collection (the umbrella that re-exports every M3E widget), and most apps reach it through stacked_kit's Kit* wrappers (e.g. KitNativePopupMenu). The root dependency_overrides path: entry is the only thing that activates the patch — m3e_collection's own version constraint is unchanged.

Features appendix

  • Two-segment split button (leading action + trailing menu)
  • Six size rows (XS-XL)
  • Four emphasis families (filled / tonal / outlined / elevated)
  • Round or square resting shape; pressed morph via tokens
  • items: list OR menuBuilder: for dynamic PopupMenuEntry lists
  • Edge-aware dropdown positioning from trailing rect (fork)Right-aligned for right-of-centre triggers, left for left-of-centre. Passes the true rect to showMenu so _PopupMenuRouteLayout picks the right side.
  • 8px vertical gap (parity with KitNativePopupMenu) (fork)Was 4 upstream; 4 read as 'touching' the chevron.
  • Flips above when no fit below (fork)Uses the same screen-fit bound showMenu uses (screen - 8 - safeArea.bottom).
  • Caps _menuMaxHeight to free space (fork)Set as a side-effect in _menuPosition; read by _openMenu's showMenu constraints. Overlap-proof even when estHeight is wrong.
  • 48x48 min tap targets per segment
  • Caret rotation on open via AnimatedRotation

Examples

example/dynamic_menu.dart

Build the menu dynamically (e.g. from a ViewModel) instead of a static items list.

SplitButtonM3E<MailAction>(
  label: 'Move',
  leadingIcon: Icons.move_to_inbox,
  onPressed: () => _move(),
  menuBuilder: (ctx) => _folders
      .map((f) => PopupMenuItem(value: MailAction(f.id), child: Text(f.name)))
      .toList(),
  onSelected: (a) => _moveTo(a),
)

Gotchas + re-sync procedure

The patch couples to Flutter's private _PopupMenuRouteLayout behaviour — specifically that it compares position.left vs position.right to pick which screen edge to anchor against. This is not a stable public API. On any Flutter SDK bump, re-test that the menu still anchors to the trailing edge for centre and right-side triggers. If _PopupMenuRouteLayout changes its side-picking rule, this patch's edge-aware logic must be re-derived.

_menuPosition reads MediaQuery.paddingOf(Overlay.of(context).context) — the overlay's context, NOT the button's. A Scaffold body consumes bottom padding (e.g. nav-bar insets); reading from the button's context under-counts and lets showMenu's clamp drag the menu back over the chevron. If you refactor the call site, preserve the overlay-context lookup.

_menuPosition is not pure — it sets _menuMaxHeight as a side-effect, which _openMenu then reads when calling showMenu(constraints: BoxConstraints(maxHeight: _menuMaxHeight)). If you cache or reorder the call, the cap is lost and a tall menu can be clamped back over the trigger.

Re-sync procedure (shared across all four forks)

When bumping upstream (fab_m3e, navigation_rail_m3e, split_button_m3e, or toolbar_m3e):

1. Bump the fork's pubspec.yaml version: and the root pubspec.yaml override comment's stated version. 2. Backfill the fork's CHANGELOG.md with the new version entry (every fork's CHANGELOG is stale — see §11). 3. Diff each patched file against the new upstream release of the same path. 4. Re-apply each // Patched (vendored fork) / // Fork patch: / // PATCH block by hand. Do NOT copy upstream over the fork blindly — the markers are your only map of what to preserve. 5. Update the root pubspec.yaml override comment if the WHY or the patched-file list changed. 6. Run the fork's flutter test in packages/<name>/, then run the consuming showcase (stacked_kit_showcase) to confirm the patched behaviour still renders.

Override hygiene (shared)

Never remove a dependency_overrides path: entry without first confirming upstream includes the fix. A "clean" flutter pub get silently reverts the fork to the pub.dev release, and the patch — including its bug fix — disappears with no compile error. The root override comment is the only durable record of why the patch exists.

Doc-gap debt every fork carries: (a) no > Vendored fork of upstream <name> <version> banner in the README; (b) stale CHANGELOG.md; (c) EmilyMonestone → EmilyMoonstone typo in issue_tracker (present in every fork's pubspec.yaml).

Decisions / ADRs

None. The fork contract is documented in the root pubspec.yaml override comment; no separate ADR was written. The private-API coupling (_PopupMenuRouteLayout) is the strongest argument for an ADR if the patch surface grows.
